title: From The Sunday Read Archive: ‘Weird Al Yankovic’s Weirdly Enduring Appeal’

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报栏目 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的几位领袖，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilron Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔隆·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在 11 月 18 日在 NYTimes.com 上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download The New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用来观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过它的。

sentences.en: Hey, my name is Sam Anderson.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我叫萨姆·安德森。

sentences.en: I'm a staff writer for The New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报杂志》的专栏作家。

sentences.en: And today, I would like to tell you about a story I wrote about someone I think is one of the great defining geniuses of our time.
sentences.zh: 今天，我想和大家分享一个故事，主角是我认为我们这个时代最伟大的天才之一。

sentences.en: And that is Weird Al Yankovic.
sentences.zh: 那就是“怪咖阿尔”扬科维奇。

sentences.en: And I'm not joking.
sentences.zh: 我不是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: For anyone who doesn't know who Weird Al is, he is the most celebrated comedy musician of all time.
sentences.zh: 对于任何不知道怪咖阿尔是谁的人，他是史上最受赞誉的喜剧音乐人。

sentences.en: He is a quote-unquote novelty artist who makes ridiculous parody songs of popular music.
sentences.zh: 他是一位所谓的“新奇艺术家”，专门创作流行音乐的荒诞恶搞歌曲。

sentences.en: He has been around since the late 70s and first hit it big with song parodies of super hits by Michael Jackson and Madonna.
sentences.zh: 他从 70 年代末就开始活跃，最初凭借对迈克尔·杰克逊和麦当娜超级金曲的恶搞一炮走红。

sentences.en: He turned Michael Jackson's Beat It into a song called Eat It.
sentences.zh: 他把迈克尔·杰克逊的《Beat It》改编成了一首名叫《Eat It》的歌。

sentences.en: And it's just like lists of food to eat.
sentences.zh: 歌词基本上就是各种要吃的食物清单。

sentences.en: And for me, certainly as a child in the 1980s, you know, I grew up like a lot of kids do, feeling insecure, feeling anxious about various things.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，尤其是在 20 年代 80 年代的童年时期，你知道的，我和很多孩子一样，成长过程中感到不安，对各种事情感到焦虑。

sentences.en: And Weird Al leaped out of the radio to me in a way that Michael Jackson and Nirvana and Madonna never did.
sentences.zh: 而怪咖阿尔以迈克尔·杰克逊、涅槃乐队和麦当娜从未有过的奇特方式，突然闯入了我的收音机。

sentences.en: And he touched something deeper, something that made that insecure, lonely little kid feel like he had a friend, feel like he had company in the world.
sentences.zh: 他触及了内心更深处的东西，让那个缺乏安全感、孤独的小男孩觉得自己拥有了一个朋友，在这个世界上有了陪伴。

sentences.en: But even as an adult, I keep listening.
sentences.zh: 但即使成年后，我依然一直在听。

sentences.en: And I find that when I'm really, really stressed out, I can put on Weird Al very loud in my house.
sentences.zh: 我发现，当我压力非常非常大时，我可以在家里把怪咖阿尔的歌声开得很大很大。

sentences.en: And it instantly makes me feel better.
sentences.zh: 它瞬间就能让我感觉好点。

sentences.en: I think part of that is like these, you know, hearkening back to childhood and this kind of nostalgic soothing.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因在于这些歌曲，你知道的，让人回想起童年以及这种怀旧的慰藉。

sentences.en: But I think a bigger part of it is, in some ways, comedy represents our moment better than any kind of serious art could.
sentences.zh: 但我认为更重要的一部分原因是，在某些方面，喜剧比任何严肃艺术都更能代表我们的时代。

sentences.en: We live in absurd times.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个荒诞的时代。

sentences.en: And so we need an absurd artiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要一个荒诞的艺术家。

sentences.en: So I have always wanted to write a profile of Weird Al my entire writing career.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我整个写作生涯中，我一直都想为怪咖阿尔写一篇人物专访。

sentences.en: And I was finally able to do it.
sentences.zh: 我终于如愿以偿了。

sentences.en: And I hope that it makes you feel a little bit better today in this crazy world.
sentences.zh: 我希望在这个疯狂的世界里，它能让你今天感觉好一点。

sentences.en: So here's my story.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的故事。

sentences.en: It's a weird, weird, weird world read by Eduardo Ballerini.
sentences.zh: 这是一个怪诞、怪诞、又怪诞的世界，由爱德华多·巴勒里尼为您朗读。

sentences.en: That sounded like real New York Times podcast stuff.
sentences.zh: 听起来真有《纽约时报》播客的范儿。

sentences.en: The New York Times app, unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用，全面解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月，甚至不需要绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能读到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》应用，获得 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: After 40 years, Yankovic is now no longer a novelty, but an institution.
sentences.zh: 经过 40 年的发展，扬科维奇不再是一个奇特现象，而变成了一种文化标志。

sentences.en: A garish, bright patch in the middle of America's pop-cultural wallpaper.
sentences.zh: 他是美国流行文化壁纸中央一块俗艳、明亮的补丁。

sentences.en: A completely ridiculous national treasure.
sentences.zh: 一个完全荒谬的国家宝藏。

sentences.en: An absurd, living legend.
sentences.zh: 一个荒诞的活着的传奇。

sentences.en: I've spent much of my life chortling, alone in tiny rooms, to Weird Al's music.
sentences.zh: 我的大部分人生都是独自在小房间里，伴随着怪咖阿尔的音乐咯咯傻笑。

sentences.en: I churned butter once or twice, living in an Amish paradise.
sentences.zh: 我生活在阿米许人的乐园里，也曾亲手打过一两次黄油。

sentences.en: LOL.
sentences.zh: 笑死我了。

sentences.en: And yet somehow, it had never occurred to me to go out and see him live.
sentences.zh: 然而不知为何，我从来没有想过要去看他的现场演出。

sentences.en: I think this is for roughly the same reason that it has never occurred to me to make my morning commute in a hot air balloon or to brush my teeth in Niagara Falls.
sentences.zh: 我想这大致是因为，我从来没想过要坐热气球去上班，或者去尼亚加拉大瀑布刷牙。

sentences.en: Parody is not the kind of music you go out to see in person.
sentences.zh: 恶搞音乐不是那种你会去现场观看的音乐。

sentences.en: It's the joke version of that music.
sentences.zh: 它是那种音乐的搞笑版本。

sentences.en: A parody concert felt like a category error.
sentences.zh: 一场恶搞音乐会感觉像是一种范畴错误。

sentences.en: Like confusing a mirror for a window.
sentences.zh: 就像把镜子当成了窗户。

sentences.en: To me, Weird Al had always been a fundamentally private pleasure.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，怪咖阿尔一直是一种纯粹私密的快乐。

sentences.en: I was perfectly content to have him living in my headphones and on YouTube and very occasionally when I wanted to aggravate my family, out loud on my home speakers.
sentences.zh: 我完全满足于让他的声音陪伴在我的耳机里、YouTube上，以及极少数我想折磨家人时在家里音箱上大声播放的时候。

sentences.en: The show was in New York, at Forest Hills Stadium, a storied outdoor arena that once hosted the U.S.
sentences.zh: 演出在纽约的森林小丘体育场举行，这是一座历史悠久的露天竞技场，曾举办过美国网球公开赛，

sentences.en: Open, as well as concerts by the Beatles, Jimi Hendrix, and Bob Dylan.
sentences.zh: 以及披头士乐队、吉米·亨德里克斯和鲍勃·迪伦的音乐会。

sentences.en: It was late July, the hottest weekend of a punishingly hot summer, and the humidity was so thick, it felt as if gravity had doubled.
sentences.zh: 那是七月下旬，这个酷热难耐的夏天最热的一个周末，空气中的湿气浓得仿佛重力都翻倍了。

sentences.en: The backs of my knees were sweating onto the fronts of my knees.
sentences.zh: 我的膝盖窝直冒汗，流到了膝盖前侧。

sentences.en: A performance in this context struck me as a heavy lift, even for a normal rock star.
sentences.zh: 在这种环境下演出，即使对一个正常的摇滚明星来说，也是一项繁重的任务。

sentences.en: For a parody rock star, it seemed basically impossible.
sentences.zh: 而对一个恶搞摇滚明星来说，这简直是不可能的任务。

sentences.en: Deep in my brain, a blasphemous little wrinkle kept wondering secretly if the concert might even be sad.
sentences.zh: 在我脑海深处，有一个大逆不道的怪念头，暗自琢磨着这场演唱会甚至可能会有点凄凉。

sentences.en: Weird Al was on the brink of turning 60, and his defining early hits,
sentences.zh: 怪咖阿尔即将迎来 60 岁生日，他标志性的早期热门歌曲——

sentences.en: Eat It, Like a Surgeon, were several decades old, which meant they were made for a version of the culture that is now essentially Paleolithic.
sentences.zh: 《Eat It》和《Like a Surgeon》已经有几十岁了，这意味着它们是为某种对现在的文化而言基本属于旧石器时代的人群而创作的。

sentences.en: Down in my sweaty palm, every ten seconds, my phone dosed out new shots of racism and bullying and disaster and alarm.
sentences.zh: 在我汗津津的手心里，每隔十秒钟，我的手机就会推送出关于种族主义、霸凌、灾难和警报的新消息。

sentences.en: I felt exhausted, on every possible level, and I assumed everyone else did too.
sentences.zh: 我在各个层面上都感到精疲力竭，我猜其他人也是如此。

sentences.en: Would anyone even show up?
sentences.zh: 还会有人来吗？

sentences.en: The answer to that, at least, was yes.
sentences.zh: 至少这个问题的答案是：会。

sentences.en: Long before showtime, the Weird Al fans started streaming in.
sentences.zh: 演出开始前很久，怪咖阿尔的粉丝们就开始源源不断地涌入。

sentences.en: The vibe was lighthearted reverence.
sentences.zh: 现场的氛围是轻松诙谐的敬意。

sentences.en: It was a benevolent Weird Al cosplay cult.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满善意的怪咖阿尔角色扮演邪教。

sentences.en: There were so many Hawaiian shirts that it felt like an elaborate code, some secret language composed entirely of loud patterns.
sentences.zh: 夏威夷衬衫多得让人感觉像是一场精心策划的密码破译，某种完全由繁复花纹组成的秘密语言。

sentences.en: Parrots, hot dogs, palm trees, flowers, cars, accordions, pineapples, whales, bananas, sunsets.
sentences.zh: 鹦鹉、热狗、棕榈树、花朵、汽车、手风琴、菠萝、鲸鱼、香蕉、日落。

sentences.en: Everyone was so floridly mismatched that they seemed paradoxically to be matching.
sentences.zh: 每个人身上的服装都华丽而不搭，以至于从某种悖论来看，它们又出奇地相配。

sentences.en: A great harmony of clashing.
sentences.zh: 这是一种冲突的美妙和谐。

sentences.en: I saw Weird Al t-shirts from ten tours ago.
sentences.zh: 我看到了来自十次巡演前的怪咖阿尔 T 恤。

sentences.en: Weird Al hats covered with Weird Al pins.
sentences.zh: 戴着怪咖阿尔徽章的怪咖阿尔帽子。

sentences.en: Every possible colorway of checkerboard vans.
sentences.zh: 各种配色方案的棋盘格万斯帆鞋。

sentences.en: Down towards the stage, hardcore fans greeted one another like relatives reunited at a wedding.
sentences.zh: 靠近舞台的地方，铁粉们像婚礼上重逢的亲戚一样互相问候。

sentences.en: Ages seemed to range from 80 to 4.
sentences.zh: 年龄看起来从 80 岁到 4 岁不等。

sentences.en: When Weird Al appeared, waggling his arms zanely, long hair flapping in the hot wind, the crowd greeted him with a surge of joy.
sentences.zh: 当怪咖阿尔出现时，他滑稽地挥舞着双手臂，长发在热风中飘扬，人群报以汹涌的欢呼声。

sentences.en: Yankovic's Hawaiian shirt was black and gold, traced with a pattern of tropical fronds.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇的夏威夷衬衫是黑金相间的，上面点缀着热带蕨类的图案。

sentences.en: He still looked oddly young, as if his face had been locked into place for copyright reasons in 1989.
sentences.zh: 他看起来依然出奇的年轻，仿佛出于版权原因，他的脸在 1989 年就被定格在了那个时候。

sentences.en: Although he no longer sports a mustache or wears glasses, he shaved and got LASIK surgery more than 20 years ago, to the dismay of some fans, the other essentials remain.
sentences.zh: 尽管他不再留小胡子也不戴眼镜——他 20 多年前就剃掉了胡子并做了激光矫视手术，这让一些粉丝感到沮丧——但其他核心特征依然如故。

sentences.en: Weird Al has a face designed for making faces.
sentences.zh: 怪咖阿尔长着一张天生适合做鬼脸的脸。

sentences.en: Large nostrils, wide forehead, bendy mouth, chin like a crescent moon.
sentences.zh: 大鼻孔、宽额头、灵活的嘴巴、月牙般的下巴。

sentences.en: His eyeballs seem somehow double-jointed, able to bulge wide or disappear into a squint.
sentences.zh: 他的眼珠子似乎有着双关节，能够睁得滚圆，或者缩成一条缝。

sentences.en: His cheekbones pop like crab apples.
sentences.zh: 他的颧骨像海棠果一样高高隆起。

sentences.en: He uses that face to mimic music world cliches.
sentences.zh: 他用这张脸来模仿音乐界的种种陈词滥调。

sentences.en: Rockstar sneer, boy band smolder, teen pop grin, gangster rap glower.
sentences.zh: 摇滚巨星的冷笑、男团成员的深情凝视、青少年流行歌手的露齿笑、说唱匪帮的怒视。

sentences.en: Onstage Weird Al sat on a wooden stool and started to snap like a lounge singer.
sentences.zh: 舞台上的怪咖阿尔坐在木凳上，开始像酒廊歌手那样打起响指。

sentences.en: With an orchestra swelling behind him, the tour was called Strings Attached.
sentences.zh: 伴随着身后管弦乐队渐强的音乐，这次巡演的名字叫“弦乐相伴”。

sentences.en: He kicked into a soulful medley of 1980s parodies.
sentences.zh: 他开始深情演绎一首 20 世纪 80 年代恶搞歌曲串烧。

sentences.en: If that does not sound great to you, if it in fact sounds like a very particular flavor of sonic hell,
sentences.zh: 如果这听起来对你来说算不上美妙，如果它实际上听起来像是一种非常奇特的音乐地狱，

sentences.en: I'm here to tell you something.
sentences.zh: 那我得告诉你一件事。

sentences.en: Weird Al was absolutely belting.
sentences.zh: 怪咖阿尔的嗓音真的是在扯着喉咙高歌。

sentences.en: He was singing the bejesus out of this ridiculous music.
sentences.zh: 他在用尽全力演唱这些荒谬的音乐。

sentences.en: I leaned back in my chair, reassessing core assumptions I'd made about life.
sentences.zh: 我靠回椅背上，重新评估了我对生活的一些核心假设。

sentences.en: Was this somehow part of the joke?
sentences.zh: 这难道也是笑话的一部分吗？

sentences.en: That Weird Al was an amazing singer?
sentences.zh: 怪咖阿尔居然是个了不起的歌手？

sentences.en: His voice was athletic and precise.
sentences.zh: 他的嗓音极具爆发力且精准无比。

sentences.en: He was rippling through intricate trills and runs.
sentences.zh: 他熟练地穿梭于复杂的颤音和音阶之间。

sentences.en: By the time he reached the medley's climax,
sentences.zh: 当串烧音乐达到高潮时，

sentences.en: Like a Surgeon, his 1985 parody of Madonna's Like a Virgin,
sentences.zh: 也就是他 1985 年恶搞麦当娜《Like a Virgin》的《Like a Surgeon》，

sentences.en: Yankovic was stretching for high notes and holding them over his head for the crowd to admire, like an Olympic weightlifter who had just snatched 500 pounds.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇开始冲击高音，并将其高高挂起供观众惊叹，就像一个刚刚完成 500 磅抓举的奥运举重运动员。

sentences.en: The show went on for two hot hours.
sentences.zh: 演出持续了两个炎热的小时。

sentences.en: The concrete theater was a convection oven powered by body heat, and Weird Al stomped and strutted and danced through the crowd, occasionally kicking his legs straight up,
sentences.zh: 水泥剧院成了一个由人体热量驱动的对流烤箱，怪咖阿尔在人群中跺脚、阔步、舞蹈，偶尔把腿笔直地踢向空中，

sentences.en: like actually vertical,
sentences.zh: 简直是垂直向上，

sentences.en: 180 degrees.
sentences.zh: 整整 180 度。

sentences.en: Sometimes he disappeared for 30 seconds, and then came bursting back on stage in a costume.
sentences.zh: 有时他会消失 30 秒，然后又换上一身服装爆发出现在舞台上。

sentences.en: Kurt Cobain,
sentences.zh: 科特·柯本，

sentences.en: Amish rapper,
sentences.zh: 阿米许说唱歌手，

sentences.en: Devo.
sentences.zh: Devo 乐队。

sentences.en: During White and Nerdy, he did donuts all over the stage on a segue.
sentences.zh: 在演唱《White and Nerdy》时，他骑着赛格威在舞台上大转圈。

sentences.en: Before long, the masses of Weird Al's famous curls were stuck to his face, and if you looked closely, you could see sweat pouring off his elbows.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，怪咖阿尔标志性的卷发就贴在了脸上，如果你仔细看，还能看到汗水顺着他的手肘往下淌。

sentences.en: The parody songs, live, were tight and hard and urgent, supplemented occasionally by video clips projected onto a giant screen of Weird Al cameos on 30 Rock and The Simpsons
sentences.zh: 现场演绎的恶搞歌曲紧凑、有力、节奏急促，偶尔辅以巨型屏幕上投影的视频剪辑，内容是怪咖阿尔在《我为喜剧狂》、《辛普森一家》

sentences.en: and the old Naked Gun movies.
sentences.zh: 以及老版《白头神探》电影中的客串片段。

sentences.en: It felt less like a traditional concert than a Broadway musical crossed with a comedy film festival, crossed with a tent revival.
sentences.zh: 与其说这是一场传统的演唱会，不如说它更像是百老汇音乐剧与喜剧电影节、再加上帐篷布道会的结合体。

sentences.en: The crowd was rolling through tantric nerdgasms, sustained explosions of belonging and joy.
sentences.zh: 全场观众正沉浸在一种类似密宗高潮般的狂喜中，那是归属感与快乐的持续爆发。

sentences.en: It felt religious.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像是一场宗教仪式。

sentences.en: Near the end of the show, during the chorus of Amish Paradise, as the entire stadium started swinging its arms in rhythm, I unexpectedly found myself near tears.
sentences.zh: 演出快结束时，在《Amish Paradise》的副歌部分，当整个体育场开始随着节奏挥舞手臂时，我出人意料地发现自己感动得快要落泪了。

sentences.en: Weird Al was dressed in a ridiculous black suit, with a top hat and a long fake beard, and he was rapping about churning butter and raising barns, and everyone was singing along.
sentences.zh: 怪咖阿尔穿着一套滑稽的黑色西装，戴着礼帽，贴着长长的假胡子，他正用说唱的方式唱着打黄油和建谷仓，每个人都在跟着合唱。

sentences.en: I could feel deep pools of solitary childhood emotion, loneliness, affection, vulnerability, joy, beginning to stir inside me, beginning to trickle out
sentences.zh: 我能感觉到内心深处那些孤独的童年情感——孤独、温情、脆弱、快乐——开始在体内涌动，开始渗出，

sentences.en: and flow into this huge common reservoir.
sentences.zh: 并汇入这个巨大的共同水库之中。

sentences.en: All the private love I had ever had for this music, for not only Weird Al's parodies, but for the originals, now it was here, outside,
sentences.zh: 我曾对这些音乐——不仅是怪咖阿尔的恶搞，还包括原作——所怀有的所有私密的爱，此刻都释放了出来，在外面的空气中，

sentences.en: vibrating through the whole crowd.
sentences.zh: 在全场观众的共鸣中震颤。

sentences.en: Weird Al had pulled off a strange emotional trick.
sentences.zh: 怪咖阿尔完成了一个奇妙的情感魔术。

sentences.en: He had brought the isolated energy of all our tiny rooms into this one big public space.
sentences.zh: 他将我们所有人独处小房间里的孤立能量，汇聚到了这个宽敞的公共空间里。

sentences.en: When he left the stage, we stomped for more, and he came back out and played Yoda, his classic revision of the kinks, Lola.
sentences.zh: 当他离开舞台时，我们跺着脚要求返场，于是他再次登台演唱了《Yoda》，这是他对雷蒙斯乐队《Lola》的经典改编版。

sentences.en: And then he left again.
sentences.zh: 然后他再次离场。

sentences.en: And I decided that this was the single best performance of any kind that I had ever seen in my life.
sentences.zh: 我决定，这是我有生以来看过的最精彩的各类表演。

sentences.en: Weird Al Yankovic was a full-on rock star, a legitimate performance monster.
sentences.zh: 怪咖阿尔·扬科维奇是一个彻头彻尾的摇滚巨星，一个名副其实的表演怪才。

sentences.en: He was not just a parasite of cultural power, but somehow, improbably, a source of it himself.
sentences.zh: 他不只是文化力量的寄生虫，而且不知为何，极其不可思议地，他本身就成了这种力量的源泉。

sentences.en: Once upon a time, there was a boy who wet his bed.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，有一个爱尿床的男孩。

sentences.en: He wet every kind of bed available.
sentences.zh: 他尿过所有类型的床。

sentences.en: Bunk beds, water beds, blow-up beds, fold-out beds.
sentences.zh: 双层床、水床、充气床、折叠床。

sentences.en: At sleepovers, he wet sleeping bags.
sentences.zh: 去别人家过夜时，他尿过睡袋。

sentences.en: If he didn't have a bed handy, sometimes he just wet his pants.
sentences.zh: 如果手边没有床，有时他就会直接尿在裤子里。

sentences.en: He was fluent in that terrible feeling, warm relief at the wrong time in the wrong place, turning into cold shame.
sentences.zh: 他对那种可怕的感觉熟门熟路——在错误的时间、错误的地点获得短暂的温暖解脱，随之而来的是冰冷的羞耻感。

sentences.en: So many mornings were so shameful.
sentences.zh: 有多少个早晨充满了羞耻。

sentences.en: This was not the boy's only problem.
sentences.zh: 这并不是这个男孩唯一的毛病。

sentences.en: He also threw up in cars, sometimes in such pungent floods that it would ruin the upholstery forever.
sentences.zh: 他还在汽车里呕吐，有时吐出的排泄物气味如此刺鼻，以至于汽车的内饰永远毁了。

sentences.en: Occasionally, he would cry at school for no obvious reason, baffling his teachers and classmates.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，他会在学校里无缘无故地哭泣，让老师和同学们感到困惑。

sentences.en: The boy's family moved a lot, which meant that he wet beds in many different houses, threw up in many different cars, and cried in many different school districts.
sentences.zh: 这个男孩的家庭经常搬家，这意味着他在许多不同的房子里尿过床，在许多不同的汽车里吐过，在许多不同的学区哭过。

sentences.en: When kids played kiss tag at recess, the boy would not be kissed.
sentences.zh: 课间休息时孩子们玩亲亲抓人游戏，这个男孩却无人问津。

sentences.en: If a girl accidentally cornered him, she would realize who it was, then turn and run away.
sentences.zh: 如果某个女孩不小心把他逼到角落，她认出他是谁后，就会转身逃跑。

sentences.en: And so the boy spent many recesses alone, on the edge of the playground, picking up trash to earn the whole class bonus points so the teacher would allow them
sentences.zh: 于是，这个男孩独自度过了许多课间休息时间，在操场边缘捡垃圾，好为全班赢得加分，这样老师就会允许他们在学年结束时

sentences.en: to watch a special movie together at the end of the year.
sentences.zh: 一起看一场特别的电影。

sentences.en: Sometimes he would stand near the play structure, hiding his uncool shoes behind a metal pole, watching the other kids play.
sentences.zh: 有时候他会站在游乐设施旁，用金属杆挡住自己那双不够酷的鞋子，看着其他孩子玩耍。

sentences.en: And he would repeat a mantra in his head,
sentences.zh: 他会在脑海里不断重复一句话：

sentences.en: I wish I could just be normal.
sentences.zh: 我多希望能像正常人一样。

sentences.en: The idea of normalcy to the boy came mostly from television.
sentences.zh: 这个男孩对“正常”的理解主要来自电视。

sentences.en: It was some vague constellation of money, crowds, hair gel, brand name jackets, and confidence.
sentences.zh: 那是金钱、人群、发胶、名牌夹克和自信交织出的模糊幻景。

sentences.en: The kind of glittering ease that animated the great American mainstream, visible in its sitcoms and movies and slow motion basketball highlights, and perhaps most of all,
sentences.zh: 那种充满美国主流文化光芒的轻松感，在情景喜剧、电影和慢动作篮球集锦中随处可见，而也许最浓墨重彩的，

sentences.en: in its music videos.
sentences.zh: 则是音乐录影带。

sentences.en: Weirdness, by contrast, meant everything in his own life.
sentences.zh: 与此相反，怪异意味着他生活的全部。

sentences.en: Chubbiness, loneliness, boredom, clunky glasses, off-brand clothing, frozen bananas dipped in carob, lawn darts in his grandmother's backyard.
sentences.zh: 肥胖、孤独、无聊、笨重的眼镜、杂牌服装、裹着角豆树粉的冻香蕉，以及祖母后院里的草地飞镖。

sentences.en: The bed-wetting boy, dear reader, was me.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的读者，那个尿床的男孩就是我。

sentences.en: And I tell you this story not just for sympathy, although there is that, but because it was in this era that I first encountered the music of Weird Al Yankovic.
sentences.zh: 我给你讲这个故事不只是为了求得同情，虽然确实有这成分，而是因为正是在那个时期，我第一次接触到了“怪人阿尔”扬科维奇的音乐。

sentences.en: Weird Al, it seemed to me, had a perfect sense of humor.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，“怪人阿尔”有着完美的幽默感。

sentences.en: He shrieked on MTV, squeaked rubber chickens, and punctuated his songs with percussive belching.
sentences.zh: 他在MTV里尖叫，捏响橡胶鸡，还在歌曲中穿插打击乐般的打嗝声。

sentences.en: But he was more than just funny.
sentences.zh: 但他不仅仅是搞笑。

sentences.en: Even as a child, I understood on some intuitive level that Weird Al was not merely the Shakespeare of terrible food puns, might as well face it, you're addicted to spuds,
sentences.zh: 甚至在孩童时期，我就在某种直觉层面上明白，“怪人阿尔”不单单是烂俗食物双关语的莎士比亚——比如“不妨面对现实，你对土豆上瘾了”——

sentences.en: or an icon of anti-style, poodle-fro, enormous glasses, questionable mustache,
sentences.zh: 也不是反潮流的偶像、爆炸头、巨大的眼镜、可疑的小胡子、

sentences.en: Hawaiian shirts, but a spiritual technician doing important work down in the engine room of the American soul.
sentences.zh: 夏威夷衬衫，而是一位在美利坚灵魂深处的机舱里从事重要工作的精神技师。

sentences.en: I could not have said why, but I felt it.
sentences.zh: 我说不出原因，但我能感受到。

sentences.en: As his name suggested,
sentences.zh: 正如他的名字所示，

sentences.en: Weird Al's comedy operated right at the hotspot of my childhood agonies, weirdness versus normalcy, insider versus outsider.
sentences.zh: “怪人阿尔”的喜剧恰好切中了我的童年痛点：怪异与正常，局内人与局外人。

sentences.en: What a Weird Al parody did was enact a tiny revolution.
sentences.zh: “怪人阿尔”的恶搞本质上是一场微型革命。

sentences.en: It took the whole glamorous architecture of American mainstream cool,
sentences.zh: 它拿走了美国主流酷文化的宏大建筑——

sentences.en: Michael Jackson's otherworldly moves,
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·杰克逊超凡脱俗的舞步、

sentences.en: Madonna's sexual taboos, and extracted all of the coolness.
sentences.zh: 麦当娜的性禁忌，并抽离了其中所有的酷劲。

sentences.en: Into that void,
sentences.zh: 在这片真空之中，

sentences.en: Weird Al inserted the least cool person in the world,
sentences.zh: “怪人阿尔”塞进了世界上最不酷的人，

sentences.en: himself, and by proxy, all the rest of us weirdos, along with our uncool lives.
sentences.zh: 也就是他自己，并推而广之，代表了我们这群不酷的怪胎，以及我们不够酷的生活。

sentences.en: Beat It, the ubiquitous super hit about avoiding street violence, became Eat It, a nasally monologue about picky eating.
sentences.zh: 那首无处不在、关于避免街头暴力的超级热门单曲《Beat It》（走开），变成了《Eat It》（吃掉它），一首关于挑食的鼻音独白。

sentences.en: Have a banana, have a whole bunch, it doesn't matter what you had for lunch, just eat it.
sentences.zh: 吃根香蕉吧，吃上一大串，午饭吃了什么并不重要，吃就是了。

sentences.en: I Love Rock and Roll, a churning anthem of hard living and the devil's music, became I Love Rocky Road, a squawking peon to stuffing your face with ice cream.
sentences.zh: 《I Love Rock and Roll》（我爱摇滚乐）这首翻滚着硬核生活与魔鬼音乐的颂歌，变成了《I Love Rocky Road》（我爱落基山之路），一首关于狂塞冰淇淋的刺耳赞歌。

sentences.en: It is no accident that much of Yankovic's music was about food.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇的很多音乐都与食物有关，这绝非偶然。

sentences.en: Everyone ate food, every day, celebrities and nerds alike.
sentences.zh: 每个人每天都要吃东西，无论是名人还是书呆子。

sentences.en: It was the great equalizer.
sentences.zh: 食物是伟大的拉平者。

sentences.en: The switcheroo was, for me, thrilling.
sentences.zh: 这种乾坤大挪移对当时的我觉得无比震撼。

sentences.en: I would sit there with my brother in our unglamorous living room, in a town where Michael Jackson would never even consider performing, and I would feel dorkily empowered.
sentences.zh: 我和哥哥坐在我们那间毫无光彩的起居室里，身处一个迈克尔·杰克逊绝不会考虑去表演的小镇，我却感到了一种书呆子式的力量赋能。

sentences.en: Weird Al had flipped the polarities of weirdness and normalcy.
sentences.zh: “怪人阿尔”颠倒了怪异与正常的极性。

sentences.en: We had made it into the TV.
sentences.zh: 我们登上了电视。

sentences.en: We were normal.
sentences.zh: 我们是正常的。

sentences.en: Weird Al has now been releasing song parodies for seven presidential administrations.
sentences.zh: “怪人阿尔”至今已经历过七届美国总统任期，一直在发布歌曲恶搞作品。

sentences.en: He has outlasted two popes and five Supreme Court justices.
sentences.zh: 他熬过了两任教皇和五位最高法院大法官。

sentences.en: He is one of only five artists, along with his early muses,
sentences.zh: 他是仅有的五位在过去四代中的每一个十年里都有单曲进入前40强的艺术家之一，与他的早期灵感缪斯一样，

sentences.en: Michael Jackson and Madonna, to have had a top 40 single in each of the last four decades.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·杰克逊和麦当娜并列。

sentences.en: Yankovic has turned out to be one of America's greatest renewable resources.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，扬科维奇是美国最伟大的可再生资源之一。

sentences.en: He is a timeless force that expresses itself through hyperspecific cultural moments, the way heat from the center of the earth manifests on the surface through the particularity
sentences.zh: 他是一种永恒的力量，通过超具体的文化时刻来表达自己，就像地球中心的热量通过间歇泉的独特性在表面显现出来一样，

sentences.en: of geysers.
sentences.zh: 喷涌而出。

sentences.en: In 1996, after Coolio's
sentences.zh: 1996年，在库里奥的

sentences.en: Gangsta's Paradise became a national earworm,
sentences.zh: 《Gangsta's Paradise》（匪帮天堂）成为全国洗脑神曲后，

sentences.en: Weird Al took its thumping beat in its heavenly choir and turned it into
sentences.zh: “怪人阿尔”抓住了它那动感的节拍和神圣的唱诗班，将其改编成了

sentences.en: Amish Paradise, a ridiculous banger about rural chores.
sentences.zh: 《Amish Paradise》（阿米什天堂），一首关于田园杂务的荒诞神曲。

sentences.en: When chameleonaires
sentences.zh: 当变色龙般的

sentences.en: Raiden hit number one in 2006,
sentences.zh: 蕾哈娜在2006年登上榜首时，

sentences.en: Weird Al took a rap about driving in a car loaded with drugs and translated it into a monologue about the glories of being a nerd.
sentences.zh: “怪人阿尔”把一首关于开着装满毒品的汽车的饶舌歌，翻译成了一段赞美书呆子荣耀的独白。

sentences.en: Whatever is popular at the moment,
sentences.zh: 无论当时流行什么，

sentences.en: Yankovic can hack into its source code and reprogram it.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇都能切入其源代码并重新编程。

sentences.en: His work has inspired waves of creative nerds.
sentences.zh: 他的作品激发了一波又一波富有创造力的书呆子。

sentences.en: Andy Samberg, the actor and a member of the comedy group
sentences.zh: 演员兼喜剧团体“孤岛乐队”成员安迪·萨姆伯格

sentences.en: The Lonely Island, told me that he grew up having Weird Al dance parties with his family.
sentences.zh: 告诉我，他从小就和家人一起开“怪人阿尔”舞会。

sentences.en: Each new generation of younger kids is like, wait, this can exist?
sentences.zh: 每一代年轻的小朋友都会觉得，天哪，这居然也能存在？

sentences.en: Samberg said.
sentences.zh: 萨姆伯格说。

sentences.en: Lin-Manuel Miranda, a Weird Al obsessive, credits Yankovic as an influence on Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 林-曼努埃尔·米兰达是“怪人阿尔”的狂热粉丝，他认为扬科维奇对《汉密尔顿》产生了影响。

sentences.en: Miranda once lip-synced
sentences.zh: 米兰达曾在六年级全班同学面前对口型表演过

sentences.en: Taco Grande, a Mexican food-themed parody of the 1990 hit
sentences.zh: 《Taco Grande》，一首以墨西哥食物为主题的1990年热门歌曲

sentences.en: Rico Suave, in front of his sixth grade class.
sentences.zh: 《Rico Suave》的恶搞版。

sentences.en: He told me that he prefers many Weird Al songs to the originals.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他其实更喜欢“怪人阿尔”的许多歌曲，而不是原曲。

sentences.en: Weird Al is a perfectionist,
sentences.zh: “怪人阿尔”是个完美主义者，

sentences.en: Miranda said.
sentences.zh: 米兰达说。

sentences.en: Every bit as much as Michael Jackson or Kurt Cobain or Madonna or any artist he has ever spoofed.
sentences.zh: 这一点完全不亚于迈克尔·杰克逊、科特·柯本、麦当娜，或是他恶搞过的任何一位艺术家。

sentences.en: So you get the musical power of the original along with this incredible twist of Weird Al's voice and Weird Al's brain.
sentences.zh: 所以你既能获得原曲的音乐力量，又能体味到“怪人阿尔”的声音和大脑带来的不可思议的奇妙扭转。

sentences.en: The original songs lose none of their power, even when they're on a polka with burping sound effects in the background.
sentences.zh: 原曲的能量丝毫没有减弱，即使它们被融进带有背景打嗝音效的波尔卡舞曲中也是如此。

sentences.en: In fact, it accelerates their power.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这反而放大了它们的能量。

sentences.en: It's both earnest and a parody.
sentences.zh: 它既真诚又是恶搞。

sentences.en: Michael Schur, the creator of The Good Place and co-creator of Parks and Recreation, remembers the force of Weird Al's
sentences.zh: 《善地》主创兼《公园与游憩》联合主创迈克尔·舒尔，回忆起“怪人阿尔”在

sentences.en: 1992 parody of Nirvana.
sentences.zh: 1992年恶搞涅槃乐队时产生的巨大冲击。

sentences.en: Smells Like Teen Spirit comes out, and it's like the perfect voice for all the simmering anger of an entire generation of kids,
sentences.zh: 《Smells Like Teen Spirit》一问世，就像是整代孩子内心的隐忍愤怒找到了完美的代言声音，

sentences.en: Schur said.
sentences.zh: 舒尔说。

sentences.en: That song is vicious and angry and aggressive, but also laconic and disaffected and scary, and it was immediately a gigantic thing in American culture.
sentences.zh: 那首歌充满恶毒、愤怒与攻击性，但同时也显得冷漠、疏离而又吓人，它瞬间成为了美国文化中的庞然大物。

sentences.en: Then Weird Al does Smells Like Nirvana and completely deflates it, the importance and seriousness and angSt.
sentences.zh: 然后“怪人阿尔”创作了《Smells Like Nirvana》（闻起来像涅槃），彻底消解了那种重要性、严肃感和青春期的焦虑。

sentences.en: That's a service he has always provided to remind people that rock is about grittiness and authenticity and finding your voice and relating to an audience, but it's also
sentences.zh: 这是他一直在提供的一种服务：提醒人们摇滚乐关乎粗粝感、真实性、寻找自我声音以及与观众共鸣，但它同时

sentences.en: fundamentally absurd.
sentences.zh: 也是极其荒诞的。

sentences.en: Being a rock star is stupid.
sentences.zh: 当摇滚巨星是很蠢的。

sentences.en: We as a culture are genuflecting at the altar of these rock stars, and Weird Al comes out with this crazy curly hair and an accordion, and he just blows it all into smithereens
sentences.zh: 我们作为一种文化在这些摇滚巨星的圣坛前頂礼膜拜，而“怪人阿尔”顶着一头疯狂的卷发拿着手风琴出场，通过唱起垃圾邮件，把这一切轰得粉碎

sentences.en: by singing about spam.
sentences.zh: 炸成齑粉。

sentences.en: It's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: Schur paused.
sentences.zh: 舒尔停顿了一下。

sentences.zh: 他没有什么需要洗刷的坏名声，也没有什么史诗级的丢人经历，于是他决定实施一次品牌重塑。

sentences.en: He introduced himself to everyone not as Alfred, but as Al.
sentences.zh: 他向所有人介绍自己时不叫阿尔弗雷德，而是叫阿尔。

sentences.en: Alfred sounded like the kind of kid who might invent his own math problems for fun.
sentences.zh: 阿尔弗雷德听起来像是那种会为了好玩而自己发明数学题的孩子。

sentences.en: Al sounded like the opposite of that.
sentences.zh: 阿尔听起来则完全相反。

sentences.en: A guy who would hang out with the dudes, eating pizza, casually noodling on an electric guitar, tossing off jokes so unexpectedly hilarious they would send streams of light beer
sentences.zh: 一个会和哥们儿闲混、吃比萨、漫不经心地弹着电吉他、抛出让人始料未及的爆笑段子，以至于能让淡啤酒从每个人的鼻子里

sentences.en: rocketing out of everyone's noses.
sentences.zh: 喷涌而出的家伙。

sentences.en: The problem was that even at college, even under the alias of Al,
sentences.zh: 问题在于，即使在大学里，即使顶着阿尔的化名，

sentences.en: Yankovic was still himself.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇依然还是他自己。

sentences.en: He was still fundamentally an Alfred.
sentences.zh: 他本质上仍然是个阿尔弗雷德。

sentences.en: He was, in all kinds of excruciating ways, not your average freshman.
sentences.zh: 他在各种令人痛苦的方面，都绝不是你所见的那种普通大一新生。

sentences.en: He was 16.
sentences.zh: 他16岁。

sentences.en: He wore thick glasses and had a regrettable mustache.
sentences.zh: 他戴着厚厚的眼镜，留着一撇让人不敢恭维的小胡子。

sentences.en: He was skinny and pathologically shy.
sentences.zh: 他又瘦又病态地害羞。

sentences.en: He had the social skills of a ceramic frog.
sentences.zh: 他的社交能力就像一只陶瓷青蛙。

sentences.en: He didn't drink, smoke, party, date, or swear.
sentences.zh: 他不喝酒、不抽烟、不参加派对、不约会也不说脏话。

sentences.en: He still felt most comfortable alone in his tiny room.
sentences.zh: 他依然觉得独自待在自己那个小房间里最自在。

sentences.en: The other guys on his dorm floor knew Al Yankovic only as this mysterious oddball haunting the place like
sentences.zh: 他宿舍楼里的其他男生只知道阿尔·扬科维奇是个神秘的怪咖，像

sentences.en: Boo Radley.
sentences.zh: 布布·雷德利一样神出鬼没地游荡在这里。

sentences.en: They would all be hanging out, sprawled around in someone's room, door open, laughter spilling into the hallway, when suddenly this pale kid would come slumping by, off to class
sentences.zh: 大家本在某人的房间里闲聊、四仰八叉地躺着，门开着，笑声传到走廊里，突然这个面色苍白的小子就会无声无息地晃悠过去，去上课

sentences.en: or to the library, saying nothing, casting a shy glance in the door.
sentences.zh: 或者去图书馆，一言不发，往门里怯生生地瞥上一眼。

sentences.en: He often wore a variation on the same outfit, a striped shirt, a floppy bucket hat, like Gilligan on Gilligan's Island, and flip-flops even when it was raining outside.
sentences.zh: 他经常穿着同一套衣服的变体，一件条纹衫，一顶软呢渔夫帽（就像《盖里根岛》里的盖里根），甚至外面下雨时也穿着人字拖。

sentences.en: The guys would watch him pass, only very slightly interested, like a pack of lions watching a distant ibis.
sentences.zh: 小伙子们会看着他走过，只有极其微弱的兴趣，就像一群狮子看着远处的一只朱鹭。

sentences.en: An owl would look in through the open door, and there would be this monument of mutual regard, the in-group and the outcast, staring each other down.
sentences.zh: 一只猫头鹰会透过敞开的门往里看，于是便有了这种相互打量的奇观，主流群体和边缘人，彼此死死盯着对方。

sentences.en: Over time, this silent encounter became a ritual, awkward but familiar.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，这种无声的相遇变成了一种仪式，尴尬却又熟悉。

sentences.en: Eventually,
sentences.zh: 最终，

sentences.en: Yankovic started to play variations.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇开始玩出花样。

sentences.en: As he walked by, he would stare inside and make a face, screw his eyes up, lower his eyebrows, serio-comically glower.
sentences.zh: 当他走过时，他会盯着里面做个鬼脸，双眼紧闭，眉头下垂，摆出一副半开玩笑半认真的阴沉表情。

sentences.en: It was the weird guy being weird, silently acknowledging his weirdness, performing it to entertain himself.
sentences.zh: 这是怪咖在展现怪异，无声地承认自己的古怪，以此自娱自乐。

sentences.en: Once, in the fateful silence that followed, a guy in the room spoke up.
sentences.zh: 有一次，在随之而来的宿命般的寂静中，房间里的一个小伙子开口了。

sentences.en: Hey, he said, it's, expletive,
sentences.zh: 嘿，他说，那不是，（脏话），

sentences.en: Weird Al.
sentences.zh: 怪人阿尔吗。

sentences.en: This was not meant as a compliment.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是什么恭维。

sentences.en: It was an attempt to return in words the strange energy
sentences.zh: 这是试图用言语回应那种

sentences.en: Yankovic was pouring into the room through his eyes.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇通过双眼倾泻进房间的诡异能量。

sentences.en: The nickname got repeated every time he went shuffling paSt.
sentences.zh: 每次他拖沓着脚步走过时，这个外号就会被重复一遍。

sentences.en: Hey,
sentences.zh: 嘿，

sentences.en: Weird Al.
sentences.zh: 怪人阿尔。

sentences.en: And so it stuck, and slowly Al began to embrace it, to reclaim the insult as a badge of honor.
sentences.zh: 于是这个外号就叫开了，慢慢地阿尔开始接受它，将这个侮辱性的称呼重新夺回，当作一枚荣誉勋章。

sentences.en: It took him a long time to make a real friend.
sentences.zh: 他花了很长时间才交到一个真正的朋友。

sentences.en: One day,
sentences.zh: 有一天，

sentences.en: Joel Miller, one of the normal guys in the dorm room
sentences.zh: 乔尔·米勒——那个扬科维奇曾直勾勾盯着的宿舍里的正常男生之一，

sentences.en: Yankovic stared into, walked into the communal bathroom to find a group of kids laughing.
sentences.zh: 走进公共浴室，发现有一群孩子在笑。

sentences.en: He asked them what was up.
sentences.zh: 他问他们在笑什么。

sentences.en: Turns out, they had just pulled a prank on Weird Al.
sentences.zh: 原来，他们刚刚对怪人阿尔搞了一个恶作剧。

sentences.en: Knowing how cringingly awkward he was, they had sneaked in while he was showering and stolen his clothes.
sentences.zh: 深知他有多么令人尴尬地笨拙，他们趁他洗澡时偷偷溜进去偷走了他的衣服。

sentences.en: In his panic,
sentences.zh: 在惊慌失措中，

sentences.en: Weird Al had ripped down the shower curtain, wrapped himself in it, and sprinted off to his room, soaking wet.
sentences.zh: 怪人阿尔扯下了浴帘，把自己裹在里面，浑身湿漉漉地一路狂奔回了房间。

sentences.en: Miller threatened to bash the guys over the head with a chair, got Weird Al's clothes, and returned them.
sentences.zh: 米勒威胁要用椅子砸那些家伙的脑袋，拿回了怪人阿尔的衣服并还给了他。

sentences.en: This was the beginning of the longest close friendship of Al Yankovic's life, a friendship that still endures.
sentences.zh: 这是阿尔·扬科维奇一生中最长久且最亲密的友谊的开始，这份友谊至今依然延续。

sentences.en: Miller noticed the accordion in Yankovic's dorm room and asked if he actually knew how to play.
sentences.zh: 米勒注意到了扬科维奇宿舍里的手风琴，并问他是否真的会弹。

sentences.en: Yankovic said yes, he could play any song anyone wanted to hear.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇说会，任何别人想听的歌他都能弹。

sentences.en: Miller, trying to stump him, said how about
sentences.zh: 米勒为了难倒他，说来首

sentences.en: Elton John's
sentences.zh: 埃尔顿·约翰的

sentences.en: Funeral for a Friend,
sentences.zh: 《死者的葬礼》，

sentences.en: Love Lies Bleeding, an eleven minute piano rock dirge.
sentences.zh: 《爱意渐逝》，那是一首长达十一分钟的钢琴摇滚挽歌。

sentences.en: Al strapped on his accordion and played the song, note for note, all the way through.
sentences.zh: 阿尔背上他的手风琴，一音不差地把这首歌从头到尾弹了下来。

sentences.en: This earned Weird Al an invitation to hang out in the dorm room, where he played his accordion for everyone else.
sentences.zh: 这为怪人阿尔赢得了去宿舍里闲混的邀请，他在那里为其他人弹奏手风琴。

sentences.en: Miller grabbed his bongos, and the two of them jammed for hours.
sentences.zh: 米勒拿起了他的邦戈鼓，两人即兴合奏了几个小时。

sentences.en: If, in the superhero narrative of Weird Al Yankovic, there is a radioactive spider bite moment, it has to be open mic night at Cal Poly in 1977.
sentences.zh: 如果在怪人阿尔·扬科维奇的超级英雄叙事中有一个被放射性蜘蛛咬伤的时刻，那一定就是1977年在加州理工学院的开放麦之夜。

sentences.en: Imagine the scene, a bunch of long-haired idealists with banjos and acoustic guitars ready to shock the world with the beauty of their finger-picking.
sentences.zh: 想象一下那个场景，一群长发飘飘的理想主义者拿着班卓琴和木吉他，准备用他们精湛的指弹技巧震撼世界。

sentences.en: And then Weird Al steps on stage.
sentences.zh: 然后怪人阿尔走上了舞台。

sentences.en: He brought with him not only his accordion and his large glasses and his little mustache, but his whole awkward chaotic energy.
sentences.zh: 他带上台的不仅有他的手风琴、厚厚的眼镜和小胡子，还有他整个人尴尬又混乱的能量。

sentences.en: Miller set up his bongos, and together the pair launched into the exact opposite of earnest folk music.
sentences.zh: 米勒架起了他的邦戈鼓，两人一起弹奏出与一本正经的民谣完全相反的音乐。

sentences.en: Yankovic played
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇演奏了

sentences.en: Wipe Out and
sentences.zh: 《Wipe Out》和

sentences.en: Alzo Sprak Zarathustra, and a ten-minute medley that he claimed covered every song ever written in the history of the world.
sentences.zh: 《查拉图斯特拉如是说》，以及一个据他称涵盖了世界历史上创作过的所有歌曲的长达十分钟的串烧。

sentences.en: Before that night,
sentences.zh: 在那天晚上之前，

sentences.en: Yankovic's public performances included childhood accordion competitions and a cousin's wedding.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇的公开表演包括童年时的手风琴比赛以及表亲的婚礼。

sentences.en: Now he was sharing his own music, the essence of himself, with a room full of strangers.
sentences.zh: 现在，他正与满屋子的陌生人分享他自己的音乐，也就是他自己的本质。

sentences.en: The odds were high that he would bomb, then disappear back into his tiny room forever.
sentences.zh: 他演砸然后永远消失回自己那个小房间的概率极高。

sentences.en: Instead, the opposite happened.
sentences.zh: 然而，结果却恰恰相反。

sentences.en: The crowd went crazy,
sentences.zh: 全场陷入疯狂，

sentences.en: Weird Al's ridiculous music on a standing ovation.
sentences.zh: 怪人阿尔滑稽的音乐赢得了全场起立鼓掌。

sentences.en: The applause would not stop.
sentences.zh: 掌声经久不息。

sentences.en: People hollered for more.
sentences.zh: 人们大声呼喊着再来一个。

sentences.en: For a kid who had spent his whole childhood being either ignored or bullied, that sudden validation was transformative.
sentences.zh: 对于一个整个童年不是被忽视就是被欺负的孩子来说，这种突然的认可具有颠覆性的变革意义。

sentences.en: Miller remembers looking over at his shy friend and seeing Yankovic's face lit with total joy.
sentences.zh: 米勒记得自己转头看了一眼这位害羞的朋友，看到扬科维奇的脸上洋溢着纯粹的喜悦。

sentences.en: It was glowing, he once said, like Chernobyl melting down.
sentences.zh: 他曾经说过，那光芒就像切尔诺贝利核电站熔毁一样耀眼。

sentences.en: I think it was the first time
sentences.zh: 我想那是我第一次

sentences.en: I'd ever had that kind of positive reinforcement,
sentences.zh: 获得那种程度的正面反馈，

sentences.en: Yankovic told me.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇告诉我。

sentences.en: It probably did flip a switch somewhere in my head.
sentences.zh: 它可能确实在我脑海里的某处按下了开关。

sentences.en: That Chernobyl moment changed everything.
sentences.zh: 那个“切尔诺贝利”时刻改变了一切。

sentences.en: Yankovic's schoolwork began to recede.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇的学业开始退居其次。

sentences.en: He was on fire with dumb music.
sentences.zh: 他被这种愚蠢的音乐点燃了。

sentences.en: Weird Al wrote new songs constantly and played them at every venue that would have him.
sentences.zh: 怪人阿尔不断创作新歌，并在每一个愿意接纳他的场馆里进行表演。

sentences.en: He and Miller were once heckled at a fraternity barn dance.
sentences.zh: 他和米勒曾在一个兄弟会的草坪舞会上遭到嘘声嘲讽。

sentences.en: But success was coming.
sentences.zh: 但成功即将来临。

sentences.en: In 1979, during his junior year,
sentences.zh: 1979年，在他大三的时候，

sentences.en: Weird Al stood in a men's bathroom at Cal Poly, he liked the acoustics of the tile, and recorded a parody of the number one song in America, the knacks
sentences.zh: 怪人阿尔站在加州理工学院的一个男卫生间里——他很喜欢瓷砖的音响效果——录制了一首对美国头号热门歌曲的恶搞，也就是The Knack乐队的

sentences.en: My Sharona.
sentences.zh: 我的沙罗娜。

sentences.en: A lusty, humpy, cringy ode to seducing a teenage girl.
sentences.zh: 这是一首关于勾引十几岁女孩的充满色欲、发情且令人尴尬的颂歌。

sentences.en: Weird Al's version was a two-minute romp about lunch meat called
sentences.zh: 怪人阿尔的版本是一首关于午餐肉的两分钟狂欢曲，名叫

sentences.en: My Ballona.
sentences.zh: 我的巴洛纳。

sentences.en: It had a crazy
sentences.zh: 它有着一种疯狂的

sentences.en: DIY, nerd-punk energy.
sentences.zh: DIY、书呆子朋克风格。

sentences.en: You could hear
sentences.zh: 你可以听到

sentences.en: Yankovic committing every fiber of his lonely soul to the bit, crooning and grunting like a man driven insane with desire.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇倾注了他孤独灵魂的每一根纤维来演绎这段音乐，像一个被欲望逼疯的男人一样哼唱和低吼。

sentences.en: It didn't matter that the pun was bad, that the singing was raw.
sentences.zh: 双关语有多烂、唱功有多生涩都无所谓。

sentences.en: All of that was exactly the point.
sentences.zh: 所有这些恰恰就是精髓所在。

sentences.en: Dr. Demento's listeners went crazy for it, and radio stations picked it up nationwide, and the lead singer of the Knack urged Capitol Records to release the song as a 45.
sentences.zh: 德门托博士的听众为之疯狂，全国各地的广播电台纷纷播放，The Knack乐队的主唱甚至敦促国会唱片公司将这首歌作为45转唱片发行。

sentences.en: And suddenly,
sentences.zh: 突然之间，

sentences.en: Weird Al had his first recording contract.
sentences.zh: “怪人奥尔”签下了他的第一份录音合约。

sentences.en: To this day,
sentences.zh: 直到今天，

sentences.en: Cal Poly marks that bathroom with a plaque as the birthplace of Weird Al
sentences.zh: 加州州立理工大学仍在那个洗手间外立了一块牌匾，

sentences.en: Yankovic's career.
sentences.zh: 标明那是“怪人奥尔”扬科维奇职业生涯的诞生地。

sentences.en: In underground comedy circles, the legend of Weird Al began to grow.
sentences.zh: 在地下喜剧圈里，“怪人奥尔”的传奇开始发酵。

sentences.en: He became a staple on Dr. Demento's show, answering phone lines and playing his accordion in studio and generally hamming it up.
sentences.zh: 他成了德门托博士节目的常客，负责接听热线、在录音室里弹手风琴，各种活宝耍宝信手拈来。

sentences.en: He turned Queens,
sentences.zh: 他把皇后乐队的

sentences.en: Another One Bites the Dust, into Another One
sentences.zh: 《另一个咬牙切齿》改编成了

sentences.en: Rides the Bus.
sentences.zh: 《另一个挤公交》。

sentences.en: By the time
sentences.zh: 等到

sentences.en: Yankovic graduated from college, joke music was all he cared about.
sentences.zh: 扬科维奇大学毕业时，搞笑音乐成了他唯一的挚爱。

sentences.en: He hardly had time for anything else.
sentences.zh: 他几乎抽不出时间去理会别的任何事。

sentences.en: He moved to Los Angeles, slept on a couch, briefly lived in his car.
sentences.zh: 他搬到了洛杉矶，睡在沙发上，还在车里短暂住过一阵。

sentences.en: He got a minimum wage job in a mailroom.
sentences.zh: 他在收发室找了一份拿最低工资的工作。

sentences.en: He moved into a tiny apartment with a Murphy bed and a view of the Hollywood sign.
sentences.zh: 他搬进了一间极小的公寓，里面有一张墨菲隐壁床，窗外能看到好莱坞的标志。

sentences.en: He sat there by himself, recording music, building his oeuvre, joke by joke.
sentences.zh: 他独自一人坐在那里，录制音乐，创作他的作品，一个笑话接着一个笑话。

sentences.en: Sometimes he taped silverware all over the walls just to be weird.
sentences.zh: 有时候他在墙上贴满银制餐具，纯粹是为了搞怪。

sentences.en: On April Fool's Day,
sentences.zh: 在愚人节那天，

sentences.en: MTV did something preposterous.
sentences.zh: MTV电视台搞了一出匪夷所思的大动作。

sentences.en: The network, back then, was influential but also desperate for content, and Yankovic's outsider weirdo shtick killed with its audience.
sentences.zh: 那时的MTV虽然颇具影响力，但也极度渴望节目内容，而扬科维奇那种局外怪咖的风格深受观众追捧。

sentences.en: So the network gave Yankovic four hours to fill with whatever he wanted.
sentences.zh: 于是电视台给扬科维奇留出了四个小时，让他随心所欲地填满节目。

sentences.en: He created
sentences.zh: 他创作了

sentences.en: Al TV, a parody of MTV.
sentences.zh: “奥尔电视台”（Al TV），一个恶搞MTV的节目。

sentences.en: The conceit was that Weird Al had taken over the station with a pirate transmitter.
sentences.zh: 核心概念是“怪人奥尔”用海盗电台劫持了整个电视台。

sentences.en: Hour after hour, he made fun of music videos, read fake fan letters, announced fake contests, and spliced together footage of celebrities into preposterous fake interviews.
sentences.zh: 一个小时又一个小时，他恶搞音乐录影带，宣读假的歌迷来信，发布假的比赛，还将名人的采访剪辑成荒诞不经的假访问。

sentences.en: Weird Al,
sentences.zh: “怪人奥尔”：

sentences.en: Mr. George, if you were on an Arctic expedition and you got stranded, who would be the first people you'd eat?
sentences.zh: “乔治先生，如果你在北极探险时被困住了，你觉得谁会是你最先吃掉的人？”

sentences.en: Boy George, housewives, young kids.
sentences.zh: “乔治男孩、家庭主妇、小孩子。”

sentences.en: This made Weird Al a brand name on the network, a sort of stand-in for the audience itself.
sentences.zh: 这让“怪人奥尔”在电视台成了响当当的招牌，某种程度上成了观众本身的化身。

sentences.en: For many decades, he's been trying to delight Alfred Yankovic, the bright, painfully shy kid who grew up alone in his tiny bedroom.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他一直在试图取悦阿尔弗雷德·扬科维奇——那个在自己小小卧室里孤单长大的聪明、极度害羞的孩子。

sentences.en: For the benefit of that lonely boy, he reshaped the whole world of pop culture.
sentences.zh: 为了那个孤独男孩的福祉，他重塑了整个流行文化世界。

sentences.en: his ridiculous music sent out a pulse, a signal, and these were the people it drew, the odd, the left out, a crowd of friends for that lonely kid.
sentences.zh: 他荒诞的音乐发出了一种脉冲、一个信号，而这吸引了这样一群人：古怪的、被排挤的，为那个孤独孩子聚集的一群朋友。

sentences.en: As I watched him with his fans, sometimes I felt as if Weird Al was multiplying all around me, multiplying inside of me.
sentences.zh: 当看着他和粉丝在一起时，有时我觉得“怪咖阿尔”在我周围四处复制，在我体内繁衍。

sentences.en: We were one crowd,
sentences.zh: 我们是一个群体，

sentences.en: united in isolation,
sentences.zh: 在孤立中团结，

sentences.en: together in a great collective loneliness, that once you recognized it, once you accepted it, felt right on the brink of being healed.
sentences.zh: 共同沉浸在一种巨大的集体孤独感中，而一旦你认清了它，一旦你接受了它，就会觉得它正处于被治愈的边缘。
